# Foundry: Full Context Documentation

> Foundry is a persistent orchestration layer for AI-assisted software development, transforming multi-agent coding into an autonomous, deterministic software factory.

## Executive Summary

Foundry replaces chaotic, prompt-and-pray AI chat interfaces with an industrial control plane. Rather than asking an AI model to edit files directly in your main working branch, Foundry ingests high-level goals and structured task breakdowns, spawns worker agents inside isolated Git worktrees, verifies every proposed modification through multi-tiered deterministic validation (regex, AST syntax checks, unit/integration test suites), and only merges verified, passing code into clean branches and pull requests.

## Distribution Tiers

### 1. Foundry Open-Source Core (Public)
- Repository: https://github.com/ai-supervisor-foundry/foundry
- License: MIT
- Scope:
  - Standalone supervisor control loop.
  - Redis/Dragonfly task queue and state management.
  - Multi-provider AI CLI execution (Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini, Ollama).
  - Git worktree worker isolation.
  - Deterministic regex & AST validation engine.
  - Terminal CLI and local Web UI dashboard.

### 2. Foundry Enterprise Edition (Commercial License)
- Pricing: $4,999 USD (One-time Commercial License) / Upcoming Cloud SaaS
- Enterprise Capabilities:
  - Enterprise-grade multi-agent concurrency limits and parallel worktree workers.
  - Proprietary behavioral verification engines tailored for enterprise codebases.
  - Turnkey private infrastructure deployment (on-premise or dedicated cloud).
  - Custom client connectors and webhooks for Jira, Linear, and internal portals.
  - Dedicated architectural onboarding, SLA, and custom provider connector support.
  - White-label branding rights and direct priority bridge to the upcoming Foundry Cloud SaaS platform.

## Core Architecture

### Control Loop & Scheduling
1. Task Ingestion: Tasks enter the FIFO queue via the Web Dashboard, CLI, or API connector.
2. Dependency Resolution: Tasks with unfinished prerequisite dependencies remain in the waiting queue. Once prerequisites pass, tasks graduate to the ready queue.
3. Worker Allocation: A pool of concurrent worker agents checks out dedicated Git worktrees branched off origin/main.
4. Execution Sandbox: Agents run with strict filesystem path confinement and sanitized shell execution.
5. Deterministic Gateways: Proposed changes are validated with zero LLM overhead using AST pattern matching and test suites.
6. Gitops Pipeline: Only fully verified tasks are submitted via isolated branches and Pull Requests.

## API & Integration Endpoints

- Web UI & Control Plane: Served on local or reverse-proxied Traefik edge.
- API Endpoints: Task ingestion (/api/connect/tasks), state inspection, queue metrics, and provider telemetry.
